title: Black Friday's frenzy gives way to "Black November"
source: Axios — Black Friday's frenzy gives way to "Black November" (2026-11-27)
body: The days of shoppers lining up outside of stores on Thanksgiving night and fighting over the season's hottest toys are giving way to a much calmer Black Friday shopping experience. The big picture: A strategy that gained momentum during the pandemic to entice shoppers to spread out their spending has become a holiday retail staple, with businesses extending sales across weeks rather than a single day. State of play: An estimated 182.7 million consumers are expected to shop during Thanksgiving weekend, down more than 2% from last year, according to the National Retail Federation . The dip is largely attributed to Americans shopping sooner, with 60% starting their holiday shopping by early November, the federation said. The share of shoppers planning to concentrate their purchases around Black Friday also fell from 25% to 17%, a Bank of America survey found. Still, the days between Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday are expected to drive over $47.5 billion in online sales, up more than 7% from 2025, according to an Adobe Analytics forecast. The intrigue: Extended promotions have blurred the lines between Black Friday, Small Business Saturday and Cyber Monday, creating what Sheri Lambert, a marketing professor at Temple University, described as " Black November ," a month-long savings event. Holiday discounts on some electronics began creeping into early November back in 2016, a move that accelerated during the COVID-19 pandemic as consumer habits changed and online shopping surged, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics . Worth noting: AI tools are easing the holiday shopping burden , with agents that can manage gift lists, track prices, and even purchase presents. Last year, major retailers, including Target , Walmart and Amazon , launched their own smart shopping assistants to help consumers find gifts faster and secure the best deals. Yes, but: Retailers are dangling incentives to get Americans through their doors this Black Friday. Target is offering store gift cards — ranging from $25 to $100 — to the first 100 eligible guests at every store. One customer per store will receive a $1,000 card. At Bass Pro Shops and Cabela's stores, the first 250 customers ages 16 and up will receive a gift card valued between $10 and $500. JCPenney is offering a free Harry Potter Hogwarts Express mini snow globe and promoting several giveaways throughout the day with prizes that include diamond earrings and Samsonite luggage. Between the lines: A longer window to score deals doesn't necessarily mean bigger savings for shoppers — or a better shopping experience. A 2026 analysis of more than 350 Amazon products advertised as deals during Black Friday and Cyber Monday found that nearly 1 in 3 offers provided no savings at all, according to Groundwork Collaborative , an economic policy think tank. Some retailers, like Aritzia and Phoebe Philo, have added another layer to traditional Black Friday sales, offering only select customers exclusive or early access to discounted merchandise. The bottom line: With rising costs and inflation squeezing many Americans' budgets , shoppers have more time to hunt for bargains, and less reason to rush to stores on Black Friday.
